object_description: very elongated low bar parallel to the church containing a long courtyard
design_condition: the elongated low bar is inserted on the edge of the village parallel to the church to contain the exterior spaces and draw a strong boundary that completes the village around a long courtyard

positive: A very clear urban approach with an elongated low bar inserted parallel to the church
It contains the exterior spaces to create a place of meetings and activity, a new centrality
It draws a strong and assertive boundary to complete the village
The site is organised around a long courtyard between church, gymnasium and new school
The elongated low volume refers to the typical agricultural buildings of the region
By its presence it strengthens the centre of the village
A vegetable garden runs along the south facade
Circulation and class entrances are distributed linearly, offering an interior walk along the square
A northern lug for extra-curricular activities articulates the square into two outdoor spaces
This public volume functions as an attractor placed in the middle of the public space
Its purpose goes beyond a school, usable as a small village hall for all kinds of events
The jury notes the clarity of the urban approach, the sobriety, readability and rationality
The fully timber above-ground structure maximises the use of the client own resources
The assembly presents great simplicity and rationality for vertical and horizontal loads
The cement screed gives good thermal inertia
The roof geometry creates a thermal buffer zone in case of overheating
Large eaves protect the facades and reduce maintenance costs
negative: Only a uniform mineral covering covers the courtyard, which does not enhance the spatial quality
The proposed school extensions complicate the volume and lose the initial plastic force
Doubts about completing the village with a bar perpendicular to the valley
The place and the school courtyard will be in the shade and in the wind
Visual breakthroughs to the south will be absent
The simple form cannot manage all site constraints of public space, routes, views and sunshine
The jury regrets the lack of permeable or planted surfaces
Access from the parking lot to the building is not convincing
The water mirror would be better located on the village square and the games space seems undersized
The chosen tree seems out of context
The topographical relationship between levels lacks resolution, giving a two-dimensional landscape project
An additional vertical escape route will need to be introduced
